selected.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create ONE polished high-fidelity desktop website homepage screenshot for Desheng Kong's personal applied-AI portfolio. This is an M0 STATIC VISUAL CONCEPT, not a live product. Straight-on flat web page, full bleed, no laptop/phone hardware, no browser chrome, no collage of multiple pages. Target canvas 1536 x 2048 portrait, showing a coherent desktop full page at wide desktop proportions. Large readable English typography and careful spacing are paramount.

ART DIRECTION: sophisticated editorial portfolio, warm white / very pale cool-gray canvas (#F7F8FA), near-black ink (#17212B), cobalt blue accent (#285DCC), restrained sage status accents, thin gray keylines. Clean Swiss typographic grid, modern humanist/geometric sans, very large confident left-aligned headline, small monospaced overlines, generous whitespace. Mostly flat, crisp interfaces, corners 12–16px, very subtle shadows only in illustrated product artifacts. No purple gradients, no neon glow, no generic glassmorphism, no emoji, no robot mascot, no fake portrait, no metrics, testimonials, client logos or partnership badges.

LAYOUT:
1. A neat horizontal top navigation within generous 90px side margins. Left wordmark "Desheng Kong". Right nav "Work" "About" and a small dark "Get in touch" button. Subtle bottom hairline.
2. Spacious two-column hero. Left around 58% width. Small overline "APPLIED AI · MELBOURNE". Main headline in very large black type with deliberate line breaks:
"AI systems."
"Built for"
"real work."
Keep the headline dominant and beautifully typeset. Below, two readable lines:
"I connect AI capabilities, product interfaces"
"and everyday workflows."
Primary cobalt button "Explore selected work" with a small downward arrow. Secondary plain text "About me" with a fine arrow.
Right side a refined original abstract system illustration: three overlapping flat white interface sheets within a pale blue architectural grid, connected by precise lines. Short tiny labels "Interface", "Knowledge", "Workflow". A small voice waveform and tiny document rows, without fabricated real-world metrics or actual application data. Small caption "ILLUSTRATIVE SYSTEM VIEW". This is a tasteful supporting visual, not a dashboard someone can mistake for production proof.
3. A narrow skills strip under the hero separated by hairlines. Four text groups: "Voice & RAG", "Workflow automation", "Applied AI", "Web interfaces".
4. Section heading "Selected work" large, and one short subtitle "Applied AI, practical tools and the work behind them." On the right a small text link "All projects".
5. Four beautifully composed project cards in a two-column grid. Each card has a wide concept thumbnail, then visible textual status badge, title, one concise description, and "View case study" plus diagonal arrow. Do not use real customers, real locations, real network diagrams, or any fake photographs. Make the four thumbnails distinct but part of one design family:
- Card 1: navy illustration of a minimal kiosk screen and abstract voice waveform, clearly captioned "Concept illustration". Title "Virtual Concierge"; badge "FIELD-TESTED"; description "Voice, knowledge retrieval and a kiosk interface."
- Card 2: pale blue synthetic portal UI illustration with left navigation and clear banner "DEMO DATA". Title "AI Platform & Customer Portal"; badge "DEMO"; description "A clear journey from access to request testing."
- Card 3: pale neutral illustration of editable poster sheets next to a simple review list. Title "Media & Visual Tools"; badge "IN DEVELOPMENT"; description "Content workflows with human review built in."
- Card 4: dark slate abstract local workspace with orderly document/task rows. Title "iClaude Workbench"; badge "IN DEVELOPMENT"; description "Project context, next steps and controlled handoffs."
6. Closing clean contact section with ample spacing. Text "Have a practical AI problem to solve?" followed by bigger "Let's talk." and a cobalt "Get in touch" button.
7. Very small footer "Desheng Kong" on left and "M0 · VISUAL CONCEPT" on right.

DESIGN CONSTRAINTS: This is a public portfolio, not a SaaS dashboard. The viewer's journey is learn who Desheng is -> inspect work -> understand contribution -> get in touch. No login, pricing plan selection, billing, admin UI, credentials, customer names, revenue, uptime, user counts or claims that every project is live. FIELD-TESTED is limited to Virtual Concierge; the portal must say DEMO; the last two remain IN DEVELOPMENT. Preserve all key English copy accurately; do not invent additional body paragraphs. Every section must fit the image cleanly, no clipped words or overflow. The final should look like a carefully designed, implementable Next.js portfolio, not a marketing mockup photographed on a device.

Use case: ui-mockup.
Using the supplied homepage image ONLY as the visual design-system reference, generate ONE matching desktop CASE STUDY page screenshot for the same personal portfolio. Do not alter the homepage; create a new page in its visual family. Straight-on flat full-bleed website, no physical device frame, no browser chrome, no multi-page collage. Target 1536 x 2048 portrait full desktop page. Preserve the reference's warm-white/very pale gray canvas, near-black large typography, cobalt-blue accents, thin gray keylines, 12px card corners, monospaced status labels, generous margins and calm technical editorial feel.

The page is an M0 visual concept for Desheng Kong's portfolio, NOT the actual client portal and NOT a live API service. All portal visuals are illustrative and synthetic. This is a project story about individual contribution, not a sales page. Do NOT use customer logos, real users, account names, raw keys, internal IPs or topology, pricing, payments, product usage metrics, uptime, awards, percentages, dates, or success claims not provided.

STRUCTURE AND PRECISE SHORT COPY:
- Top nav identical to reference: "Desheng Kong" left; "Work", "About", dark "Get in touch" button right.
- Fine text back link "← Selected work".
- Compact cobalt-bordered status "DEMO · SYNTHETIC DATA".
- Big headline over two lines: "AI Platform &" / "Customer Portal".
- Readable short introduction: "Turning platform capabilities into a clear customer journey." Second short line: "From access and usage to request testing."
- Two buttons: cobalt "View demo ↗" and secondary "Get in touch". These represent future portfolio links, NOT live API controls.
- Slim metadata row separated by hairlines: "ROLE" / "Scope, interface & integration" ; "FOCUS" / "Customer experience" ; "STAGE" / "Demonstration".

- A large beautiful pale-blue showcase panel occupying about one quarter of page height. Inside is an original synthetic portal interface preview, visually consistent with the small portal thumbnail in reference but not pretending to be a real screenshot. Left sidebar short labels: "Overview", "API keys", "Usage", "Models", "Playground", "Docs". In the content area a VERY CLEAR blue banner "DEMO DATA · NO LIVE API". Below two side-by-side simple modules: "Request playground" with a neutral text entry area labeled "Sample request" and a small button "Simulate request"; and "Response preview" with three short code-like lines "status: simulated", "source: fixture", "mode: demo". Beneath a simple sample table with non-numeric placeholders "Example request" / "Simulated". No charts, no money, no numeric model performance. Small caption directly below whole showcase: "Illustrative interface · synthetic data".

- Section title "My contribution". A three-column readable section with modest numbered headers (01/02/03 are section numbers, not metrics), short bold titles and no long paragraph:
"Product scope"
"Defined the customer journey across access, usage and request testing."
"Interface & interactions"
"Shaped navigation, responsive layouts and clear success and failure states."
"Integration boundary"
"Kept the customer interface separate from internal administration."
- Section title "What the demo shows". Three concise checklist lines:
"Create and revoke demo keys"
"Explore sample usage and export CSV"
"Run simulated requests and inspect failures"
- An obvious but elegant pale amber boundary notice with small icon. Heading "A clear boundary". Text "Synthetic data only. No live API access, real customer accounts, billing or production inference."
- A small closing row "Have a similar problem to solve?" and blue "Get in touch" button.
- Footer "Desheng Kong" left, "M0 · VISUAL CONCEPT" right.

Keep exact words readable and clean, prioritize hierarchy over tiny detail. Entire design must fit in frame without clipped footer. All text and banners should respect the fixture-only prototype boundary. Do not invent a deployed production dashboard, and do not introduce additional products, features or claims.

Use case: ui-mockup. Responsive-layout correction.
Image 1 is the mobile layout EDIT TARGET. Image 2 is the approved-for-consistency desktop STYLE REFERENCE only, not user approval.
Correct the mobile page into a truly readable narrow-phone screenshot. Preserve the same name, visual identity, warm white background, cobalt blue, near-black typography and short English content. The current Image 1 fails because its project image and description sit side by side, making text too small. Fix that.

Create a SINGLE flat mobile web page excerpt at 390 CSS pixels width and around 1120 CSS pixels height, rendered sharply at approximately 780 x 2240. No hardware frame, no browser chrome, no multiple screens. Show only the page top and the FIRST TWO project cards. Other projects continue below the visible excerpt and do not need to fit. Do not compress four cards into this image. Make body text visibly equivalent to 16–18 CSS px, card titles 23px, status badges 12–13px, headline 50px, buttons 16px with 48px height. Every project card MUST be one vertical box: FULL-WIDTH image at top, followed by FULL-WIDTH status badge, title, short sentence and link. Absolutely no horizontal image/text pairing, no two-column grid anywhere.

Detailed content and hierarchy:
- Header "Desheng Kong" at left and a simple menu icon at right, 22px side margins.
- Small uppercase overline "APPLIED AI · MELBOURNE".
- Large bold headline on three lines: "AI systems." / "Built for" / "real work."
- Readable short paragraph: "Applied AI, practical tools and clear workflows."
- Full-width blue button "Explore my work ↓". Small secondary link "Get in touch →".
- OMIT the large technical hero diagram on mobile. Replace it with a quiet three-item text strip "AI" / "Interfaces" / "Workflows" separated by fine dots or rules. This frees vertical space and is a deliberate responsive simplification.
- Clear section title "Selected work".
- Smaller but readable line "Real applications. Demos. Work in progress."
- CARD ONE: full-width navy conceptual kiosk/waveform thumbnail across top, height about 140 CSS px. Tiny caption inside "Concept illustration". Under image in separate white text block: small badge "FIELD-TESTED"; title "Virtual Concierge"; short body "Voice + knowledge integration"; link "View case study ↗". All left aligned, generous padding, no split columns.
- CARD TWO: full-width pale-blue synthetic portal thumbnail across top, height about 140 CSS px, clear banner "DEMO DATA". Under image separate full-width white block: badge "DEMO"; title "AI Platform & Customer Portal" may wrap naturally; short body "Access, usage and request testing"; link "View case study ↗".
- A tiny neutral outside-page-like annotation at the bottom "M0 · MOBILE CONCEPT · PAGE CONTINUES".
Do not add the footer contact CTA, third or fourth card, extra paragraphs, proof metrics, dates, customer data or anything that shrinks these readable elements. Maintain visual consistency with desktop reference. Straight flat clean website screenshot, no collage, no tiny unreadable body copy, no fake production evidence.

Same near-white/pale gray background, near-black modern sans typography, cobalt accent, thin hairlines, 12px rounded panels, small monospaced status badges. "real work."
